title: Thiriet by TDS wins at Imola on the Oreca 05's first victory
dek: Starting ninth after a qualifying spin, Pierre Thiriet, Ludovic Badey and Tristan Gommendy won the 4 Hours of Imola by 12.140 seconds from Murphy, after pole-sitting JOTA lost time with damage.

chapters.title: A new Oreca and two new Russian prototypes arrive in Italy
text: The 4 Hours of Imola on 17 May 2015 was the second round of the European Le Mans Series, held at the Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari. The LMP2 class that makes up the overall order had opened its season at Silverstone with a win for Greaves Motorsport, whose Gibson 015S-Nissan had come out on top of a fierce, at times physical, three-way fight with the JOTA Sport Gibson and the Thiriet by TDS Oreca. That battle was still being talked about in the paddock, and Greaves drivers Jon Lancaster and Bjorn Wirdheim arrived with Wirdheim openly talking about winning the championship.

Eleven LMP2 cars were entered. The headline newcomers were the two SMP Racing BR01-Nissans, which made their competitive debut at Imola after more than 7,000 km of testing, including a 24-hour endurance simulation at Paul Ricard; team principal Benjamin Durand said the aim was to extract more pace now that the car was homologated, ahead of the Le Mans test day on 31 May. Thiriet by TDS was running the new Oreca 05-Nissan, still looking for its first win in what was only its third race. Weather shaped the build-up as well: Saturday morning brought cool, intermittent heavy rain, and the first free practice was run on a wet track. Thiriet by TDS topped it, with a lap of 1:41.531 after the quicker time of the Greaves car was removed. In the drier second session Thiriet by TDS went quickest again with a 1:35.181, almost a second clear of Albuquerque's JOTA Gibson (1:36.056), with the Murphy Prototypes Oreca 03R third and the Krohn Racing Ligier JS P2 fourth.

chapters.title: Albuquerque takes pole by a second and a half
text: Sunday morning was sunny and warm, and Filipe Albuquerque made the most of it. The JOTA Sport Gibson lapped in 1:34.496, 1.571 seconds quicker than anyone else, and even his second-best time was roughly seven tenths faster than the rest of the field. It was JOTA's third consecutive pole at Imola. Harry Tincknell was due to start the race.

Beside him on the front row was Nathanaël Berthon in the Murphy Prototypes Oreca 03R (1:36.067), the best of the rest by a distance. Lancaster put the Greaves Gibson third (1:36.204), narrowly ahead of Léo Roussel in the Pegasus Racing Morgan, who impressed from the start of the session. The Eurasia Motorsport Oreca of Nico Pieter de Bruijn and the Ibanez Racing Oreca of Ivan Bellarosa, who spun at Variante Alta, filled the third row, with the two SMP Racing BR01s seventh and eighth.

The fastest car of the weekend was missing from the front. After a lap aborted because an LMP3 car spun at Rivazza, Tristan Gommendy went off into the gravel at Acque Minerali in the Thiriet by TDS Oreca 05 on his next attempt, having just set the quickest first sector. The car would start ninth, with its Dunlop tyres gravel-rashed. Tracy Krohn put the Krohn Ligier tenth and Yutaka Yamagishi's Ibanez car completed the LMP2 grid in eleventh, a thousandth of a second behind.

chapters.title: Tincknell pulls away while Thiriet climbs
text: Tincknell led from pole in sweltering conditions and had opened an 18-second gap within the first half hour. Behind him Pierre Thiriet started his run through the field. From ninth, he picked off Nicolas Minassian's SMP BR01, Roussel's Pegasus, Patterson's Murphy and Wirdheim's Greaves in turn to lift the Oreca 05 into second place, and he did so on tyres that still carried the damage from Gommendy's qualifying excursion.

The first Safety Car came on lap 19, to clear gravel spread on the track, and it helped the chasing pack. Thiriet handed over after 52 minutes, and Ludovic Badey stepped into the car on fresh Dunlops to set a purple first sector straight away, passing Roussel and then getting involved with Gary Hirsch's Greaves Gibson.

chapters.title: Dolan's damage hands the lead to Thiriet by TDS
text: Tincknell handed to Simon Dolan on the 90-minute mark and the JOTA still led, but the Oreca emerged from its second stop only about 12 seconds adrift, with Badey in sight of the Gibson. The race turned shortly before half distance. Dolan, working through GT traffic, was forced off line, bounced over the Variante Alta kerbs and broke part of the left-front bodywork. At the same time a stalled Villorba Corse Ginetta had to be retrieved from the pit lane entry, bringing out the second Safety Car, and JOTA came in to replace the damaged part.

By the two-hour mark the Thiriet by TDS Oreca led, 22 seconds clear of Michael Lyons in the Murphy Oreca 03R. Murphy had run well through the opening phase, with Mark Patterson, aged 63, defending Berthon's front-row place against younger rivals before Lyons took over and held off a charging Hirsch. Badey stretched away after the restart to build a gap of about 16 seconds before Gommendy took over.

chapters.title: Gommendy controls from the front
text: On fresh Dunlops Gommendy put in a series of rapid laps and posted the fastest lap of the race, 1:36.650, which broke the back of the opposition. From there he only had to manage the gap to Berthon, who took over the Murphy for the final stint.

Behind them, JOTA's afternoon stayed untidy and Albuquerque ran third, with a late fuel splash that cost time but meant the Gibson did not have to complete an extra lap at the end. Greaves had made an early fuel stop under the first Safety Car, and Wirdheim moved the Gibson ahead of Patterson's Murphy at Tamburello; Lancaster brought it home fourth but could never get on terms with the JOTA. The Krohn Racing Ligier ran as high as second at times, and its final stint was driven on a fuel-saving map so that the car could make it with just one more stop. On the SMP side, the Mediani, Markozov and Minassian BR01 was not classified after 81 laps, while the sister car finished eighth, six laps down.

chapters.title: A 12-second win for the Oreca 05
text: Thiriet, Badey and Gommendy took the chequered flag 12.140 seconds ahead of the Murphy Oreca, completing 138 laps in the 4 hours 1 minute. It was the first win for the Oreca 05 chassis, in only its third race, and a comfortable one by the end, having started from ninth on the grid. Berthon, Lyons and Patterson were second, and the best-placed Gibson, the JOTA, finished third on the road, still on the lead lap with the winners.

Albuquerque, Tincknell and Dolan survived a post-race penalty. The car was given a 1-minute 35-second penalty, equal to a stop-and-go, because a mechanic was not wearing gloves during a pit stop, but it was not enough to drop JOTA from third. The Greaves Gibson of Hirsch, Wirdheim and Lancaster was fourth, a lap behind, with the Krohn Racing Ligier of Krohn, Niclas Jonsson and Oswaldo Negri Jr. fifth on 137 laps. The Ibanez Racing Oreca 03 of Bellarosa and José Ibanez and the Eurasia Oreca of Pu Jun Jin and de Bruijn were sixth and seventh, two laps down.

chapters.title: Oreca delivers on the Silverstone test
text: Gommendy said the performance was down to the work done at a test after Silverstone, and that he was proud of the team, his team-mates and Oreca, which he felt deserved the result. Thiriet by TDS had been fastest in both practice sessions, and the race turned that pace into a result once the qualifying spin had been overcome. Murphy Prototypes, whose Silverstone weekend had been spoiled by an electronic problem affecting the fuel system, answered with second place and gave Oreca a one-two.

The result also split the early title picture. Greaves won at Silverstone and Thiriet by TDS won at Imola, with Murphy taking second and JOTA third. The gloves penalty left the final order unchanged, and in LMP2 the top four classified cars finished within a single lap of the winner.

For Krohn Racing the fifth place was a welcome step toward the 24 Hours of Le Mans, where Tracy Krohn and Jonsson were heading for their tenth consecutive Le Mans together and their first in a prototype. SMP Racing would rebuild its cars completely after Imola before the Le Mans test day on 31 May, having used the race to collect data on the BR01. The Pegasus Morgan, which started fourth, finished 17th, nine laps down, and the second Ibanez Racing Oreca of Pierre Perret and Yamagishi was not classified.
The next round of the European Le Mans Series is the 4 Hours of Red Bull Ring in Spielberg, Austria, on 11–12 July.

facts.v: The Thiriet by TDS win at Imola was the first for the Oreca 05-Nissan in only its third race.
